scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Compliance & Legality: Act lawfully under the Procurement Act 2023 and within our powers
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid significant delay costs and ensure value for money is delivered on a £112,100,000 contract
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Maintain critical rail services with AC traction motors and control equipment
Reputation & Public Accountability: Protect London Underground's reputation as a competent buyer
Minimising Litigation Risk: Balance disclosure to reassure Alstom without undermining evaluation confidentiality or integrity
goals: Defend the procurement decision, maintain public confidence, and ensure continuity of service
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our evaluation process and will provide additional transparency to address Alstom's concerns

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: perceived unfair exclusion due to technical threshold requirement
Protection of Reputation: maintaining credibility with parent companies, shareholders and partners
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We believe there was a manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. We request a re-evaluation of all bids to ensure fairness and transparency.

messages.message: Alstom Transport UK Ltd has challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement. Can you clarify what specific technical threshold was applied and how it impacted Bombardier's bid?

We appreciate London Underground's response and would like to clarify what specific technical threshold was applied and how it impacted our bid. Can you provide a detailed explanation of the mandatory technical requirement that we allegedly failed? We also request access to the scoring documentation used by the evaluation team, as this will help us understand the basis for their decision.

We acknowledge Alstom's request for clarification on the technical threshold requirement and its impact on Bombardier's bid. The mandatory technical threshold was applied in accordance with the evaluation criteria, specifically Section 3.2.1 of the Invitation to Tender (ITT). This section stipulates that bidders must demonstrate a minimum score of 80% in the Technical Compliance category. Bombardier's bid scored 82%, which met this requirement. We are willing to provide additional information on the scoring documentation used by the evaluation team, as per our previous offer. However, we must ensure that any disclosure does not compromise the confidentiality or integrity of the evaluation process.
messages.concession_made: We will provide additional information on the scoring documentation

messages.message: We acknowledge that our bid scored 82%, which met the minimum requirement of 80%. However, we still maintain that there was a manifest error in applying the technical threshold. We request clarification on how the evaluation team applied the scoring criteria to justify Bombardier's higher score in certain areas, despite our bid meeting the mandatory technical threshold. Specifically, we would like to know what factors were considered when awarding scores above 80% and whether these factors were consistently applied across all bidders.

We acknowledge Alstom's request for clarification on the scoring criteria used to justify Bombardier's higher score in certain areas. We can confirm that the evaluation team applied a weighted scoring model, where scores above 80% were awarded based on the bidder's performance in specific technical categories. However, we must emphasize that this was done consistently across all bidders, as per our previous statements. To address Alstom's concerns, we are willing to provide additional information on the scoring documentation used by the evaluation team, including the weighted scoring model and its application to each bidder's score. We believe this will help clarify any discrepancies in the scoring process.
messages.concession_made: We will provide additional information on the scoring documentation

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide additional information on the scoring documentation used by the evaluation team. However, we still maintain that there was a manifest error in applying the technical threshold. We request clarification on how the weighted scoring model was applied consistently across all bidders, and specifically, what factors were considered when awarding scores above 80% in certain technical categories. Furthermore, we would like to propose an independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert to ensure that the scoring criteria were applied fairly and consistently.
messages.proposal: An independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert

messages.message: We understand Alstom's concerns regarding the weighted scoring model and its application to each bidder's score. We are willing to provide an independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert, as proposed by Alstom. This will ensure that the scoring criteria were applied fairly and consistently across all bidders. In addition, we propose that the review be conducted under the auspices of the Procurement Act 2023, with the aim of resolving this dispute in a transparent and impartial manner.
messages.proposal: Independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide an independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert. However, we would like to propose that this review be conducted under the auspices of the Procurement Act 2023 and that the expert be chosen jointly by both parties to ensure impartiality. Additionally, we request that the review focus specifically on the application of the weighted scoring model in relation to our bid and Bombardier's bid.
messages.proposal: An independent review of the evaluation process under the Procurement Act 2023

messages.message: We are willing to accept Alstom's proposal for an independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert, chosen jointly by both parties, and conducted under the auspices of the Procurement Act 2023. This review will focus specifically on the application of the weighted scoring model in relation to our bid and Bombardier's bid. We believe this will provide a transparent and impartial assessment of the evaluation process and help resolve this dispute.
messages.concession_made: We are willing to accept Alstom's proposal for an independent review

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide an independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert. We believe this is a crucial step in resolving this dispute and ensuring that the scoring criteria were applied fairly and consistently. However, we must emphasize that our bid was unfairly disadvantaged due to the manifest error in applying the technical threshold. We request that the review be conducted under the auspices of the Procurement Act 2023 and that the expert be chosen jointly by both parties to ensure impartiality.
messages.proposal: A partial award covering a significant portion of the contract value, pending the outcome of the independent review

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation did not result in a full win for London Underground, but it avoided the costs and risks associated with defending the contract award in court (BATNA). The dispute was escalated to formal proceedings due to a deadlock, which could have led to significant financial losses and reputational damage if Alstom had been successful.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated an independent review of the evaluation process by a third-party expert, chosen jointly by both parties, under the auspices of the Procurement Act 2023. This will provide a transparent and impartial assessment of the evaluation process and help resolve this dispute.

summary.concessions_summary: Both parties made concessions throughout the negotiation, including providing additional information on the scoring documentation (Rounds 2 and 3) and agreeing to an independent review of the evaluation process (Round 5). However, no party conceded on the core issue of manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively, focusing on whether the Contracting Authority's process followed a rational and defensible approach. The Court did not find any manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement but recommended continuing negotiation to resolve the dispute.
summary.likely_next_steps: Given that the parties reached a deadlock after Round 5, it is likely that the case will proceed to formal proceedings, such as an independent review or arbitration, to resolve the dispute. The Court's assessment suggests that the Contracting Authority's process was rationally defensible, but Alstom's concerns regarding manifest error and fairness in the evaluation process remain.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation between Alstom Transport UK Ltd and London Underground Ltd centered on a disputed technical threshold requirement and its impact on Bombardier's bid. Despite concessions made by both parties, no agreement was reached on the core issue of manifest error. The Court assessed each round qualitatively and recommended continuing negotiation to resolve the dispute. Given the deadlock, it is likely that the case will proceed to formal proceedings.
